fullPassage: Here's an application of metaphors to research papers: Below-grade-level readers in my urban middle school have a great deal of difficulty doing research. Their answer when assigned to do "a report" is to come to the media center and copy verbatim everything in the encyclopedia article or whatever source they have located, be it Internet, print, or whatever. To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, I use a comparison to a supermarket. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their "shopping list" for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format. It sometimes helps them to understand that copying everything is a wasteful endeavor.

To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, I use a comparison to a supermarket. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their "shopping list" for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format. It sometimes helps them to understand that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글의 결론: 모든 것을 베끼는 것은 낭비적인 노력이다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 모든 출처가 동등하게 중요하다: 글 전체 논지에 반대. 선별이 핵심
❌ ② 교사들이 보고서를 내주지 말아야 한다: 원문에 없는 주장
✅ ③ 모든 것을 베끼는 것은 낭비적인 노력이다: 'copying everything is a wasteful endeavor' — 글의 최종 결론. 선별적 정보 수집의 중요성
❌ ④ 학생들은 항상 인터넷을 사용해야 한다: 특정 출처 선호 없음. be it Internet, print, or whatever
det.tip: 글 전체 구조: 문제(전부 베낌) → 비유(슈퍼마켓) → 해결(쇼핑 목록) → 결론(전부 베끼기=낭비)

det.tip: be it Internet, print, or whatever: '인터넷이든 인쇄물이든 무엇이든' — 특정 출처에 한정하지 않음

주어진 단어를 올바른 어순으로 배열하시오. (영어로, 11단어)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>located</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: located = 찾아낸, 위치를 알아낸
det.analysis:
✅ ① found: 찾다 — located(위치를 알아내다/찾다)의 동의어. 'whatever source they have found'
❌ ② created: 만들다 — 출처를 '만드는' 것이 아니라 '찾는' 것
❌ ③ ignored: 무시하다 — 정반대 의미
❌ ④ memorized: 외우다 — 출처를 '외우는' 것이 아니라 '찾아내는' 것
det.tip: locate = find의 격식체. 둘 다 '찾다/발견하다' 의미
